details: Prediction market platforms Kalshi and Polymarket are expanding their offerings to include perpetual futures contracts for cryptocurrencies, US equities, and commodities. Kalshi plans to launch its crypto perpetual futures on April 27, having secured a CFTC margin trading license, while Polymarket has also announced similar plans. This move signifies increased access to leveraged crypto trading products.
title: Kalshi & Polymarket Launch Crypto Perpetual Futures

details: The exploiter behind the approximately $290 million Kelp DAO hack has begun moving a significant portion of the stolen Ether (ETH), routing about $175 million to the Ethereum mainnet and subsequently bridging funds to Bitcoin via privacy protocols like THORChain and Umbra. This action follows the Arbitrum Security Council freezing 30,766 ETH ($71 million) tied to the exploit, which is considered the largest DeFi hack of 2026.
title: Kelp DAO Exploiter Laundered $175M ETH to Bitcoin

details: Strategy (formerly MicroStrategy) has surpassed BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) to become the world's largest institutional holder of Bitcoin. Following a recent purchase of 34,164 BTC, Strategy's total holdings now stand at 815,061 BTC, exceeding IBIT's 802,824 BTC. This milestone highlights Strategy's aggressive accumulation strategy through various financial instruments.
title: MicroStrategy Becomes World's Top Bitcoin Holder

details: Bitcoin experienced a notable increase, alongside equities, after an announcement by US President Donald Trump regarding the extension of a ceasefire with Iran. This decision is seen as a stabilizing factor, alleviating geopolitical tensions and boosting market confidence, leading to positive price movements in the cryptocurrency market.
title: Bitcoin Jumps on US-Iran Ceasefire Extension News

details: New York Attorney General Letitia James has filed lawsuits against Coinbase and Gemini, alleging that their prediction market platforms operate as illegal gambling businesses under state law. The lawsuits claim these platforms allow users to bet on event outcomes, including sports and elections, without the necessary state licenses and permit users under the age of 21, violating New York's gambling regulations.
title: NY AG Sues Coinbase, Gemini for 'Illegal Gambling'
